articles.excerpt: Small contractors shouldn't have to spend hours decoding government tender documents just to discover they're missing a critical requirement. That's the problem I'm trying to solve with TenderTrap, an…
articles.body: Small contractors shouldn't have to spend hours decoding government tender documents just to discover they're missing a critical requirement. That's the problem I'm trying to solve with TenderTrap , an AI-powered tender intelligence tool that helps contractors evaluate bid opportunities before investing time and resources in preparation. What I Built Government procurement can create real opportunities for small contractors and MSMEs, but tender documents are often lengthy, technical, and difficult to evaluate. Eligibility conditions, turnover requirements, registrations, EMD, performance guarantees, and contractual clauses can all affect a bidding decision. TenderTrap converts tender PDFs into structured, evidence-backed assessments.

articles.title: FreelanceFlow: The AI Book-keeper
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle FreelanceFlow is an AI bookkeeper for freelancers that runs entirely on their own computer. Freelancers, creator…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle What I Built FreelanceFlow is an AI bookkeeper for freelancers that runs entirely on their own computer. Freelancers, creators and tiny agencies handle their own money but have no finance team. Receipts are photos, invoices are PDFs, and everything piles up. Many pay an accountant mainly to organize paperwork. A cloud AI tool could do it, but uploading client invoices and bank data to a server you don't control is exactly what a careful freelancer avoids. With FreelanceFlow, a freelancer drops in receipt images or PDFs. A local open-weight model reads them. My own validation rules flag anything doubtful.

articles.title: AI SDLC - Behaviour Validation
articles.excerpt: Georgia Kali · 17 October 2026 · AI SDLC series, IntDEx framework Why a self-reported "all tests pass" is not evidence, and how the IntDEx framework turns testing into evidence-ranked behaviour valida…
articles.body: Georgia Kali · 17 October 2026 · AI SDLC series, IntDEx framework Why a self-reported "all tests pass" is not evidence, and how the IntDEx framework turns testing into evidence-ranked behaviour validation The problem: when one model writes the code and the verdict In an AI-assisted software development lifecycle (AI SDLC), the same model can now draft the intent, the prompt, the implementation, the tests and the final test report. The IntDEx framework v5 names the risk directly: a misunderstanding can be reproduced consistently through every one of those artefacts, so "traceability then appears complete, coverage full, and validation appears good, while the entire chain is wrong". Traceability between artefacts written by one author may be internal consistency, not verification.

articles.title: Is Cloudways worth it in 2026? I ran the numbers for a small SaaS
articles.excerpt: I keep seeing "Cloudways vs raw VPS" debates. Here's what I found after running a small SaaS on both. DigitalOcean droplet: $12/month You install nginx, MySQL, PHP, SSL You configure backups (or pay $…
articles.body: I keep seeing "Cloudways vs raw VPS" debates. Here's what I found after running a small SaaS on both. The raw VPS path DigitalOcean droplet: $12/month You install nginx, MySQL, PHP, SSL You configure backups (or pay $2.40/mo extra) You patch security updates You fix it when it breaks at 3am Time cost: ~2 hours setup + 30 min/month maintenance The Cloudways path Cloudways on DigitalOcean: $14/month Same server, managed One-click staging Automated backups included Security patches applied Time cost: ~15 minutes setup + 0 maintenance The math Raw VPS: $12 + 2.5 hours of your time Cloudways: $14 + 0.25 hours If your time is worth $20/hour, raw VPS costs $62/month in real terms. Cloudways costs $19.

articles.excerpt: On Oct. 17, 2016, the Antares rocket now built by Northrop Grumman Space Systems returned to flight to come back from a catastrophic explosion. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

articles.title: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week! Here's what to expect
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, bringing a spectacular display of shooting stars to the autumn sky.
articles.body: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower.

articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
